issues.legal_issue: A plaint may be rejected for limitation at the pleading stage only when the bar appears from the plaint read as a whole and its accompanying documents.
material_facts: The defendant sought rejection of the plaint on limitation grounds under Order VII Rule 11(d) of the Code of Civil Procedure.
The plaint and documents attached to it described the agreement, the exercise of an option to renew, the denial of renewal, and the later injunction claim.
The courts considered the plaint and its annexures rather than relying on the defence to establish the limitation bar.
issues.conclusion: The limitation question could be decided under Order VII Rule 11(d) because the bar appeared from the plaint and its annexures.
issues.legal_principle: Under Order VII Rule 11(d) of the Code of Civil Procedure, a plaint may be rejected where the suit appears from its statements to be barred by law, including limitation. The plaint must be read as a whole, its averments and annexures being taken as correct; it is not permissible to isolate a sentence or add to or subtract from the pleading. The Court relied on Liverpool & London S.P. & I Association Ltd. v. M.V. Sea Success I, Popat and Kotecha Property v. State Bank of India Staff Association, T. Arivandandam v. T.V. Satyapal, and I.T.C. Limited v. Debts Recovery Appellate Tribunal.

predicates.application_to_reject_plaint: A party applies for rejection of a plaint on the ground that the suit is barred by law.
predicates.limitation_bar_apparent_from_plaint_as_a: The plaint, read as a whole with its annexures and with its averments taken as correct, shows that the suit is out of time.

issues.definition: When an application seeks rejection of a plaint and the limitation bar is apparent from the plaint as a whole, the plaint may be rejected at the pleading stage.

issues.legal_issue: Exercising an option to renew a lease does not by itself create a renewed lease where renewal requires a further instrument.
material_facts: The agreement provided for successive terms at the lessee's option.
The lessee exercised the option to renew, but the other party expressly denied that the agreement had been renewed.
No document evidencing renewal was executed, and no court declaration established that the agreement stood renewed.
issues.conclusion: The agreement was not automatically renewed by the exercise of the option; a document evidencing renewal was required.
issues.legal_principle: The Court distinguished extension from renewal: extension may continue the same lease, but renewal requires a fresh lease instrument. It relied on Provash Chandra Dalui v. Biswanath Banerjee and State of U.P. v. Lalji Tandon, and also referred to Ambika Quarries v. State of Gujarat for the principle that a renewal is a fresh grant.

predicates.lease_renewal_option_exercised: A lessee exercises an option under an existing lease to seek a further term.
predicates.renewal_claim_denied: The other party expressly denies that the lease has been renewed.
predicates.no_renewal_instrument: The parties have not executed a document evidencing renewal.

issues.definition: If a lessee exercises a renewal option, the other party denies renewal, and no renewal instrument exists, the lease is not renewed by exercise of the option alone.

issues.legal_issue: An injunction enforcing negative covenants in a renewed agreement cannot be granted without establishing that the agreement subsists, and a time-barred renewal claim cannot be avoided by framing the suit as one for injunction.
material_facts: The suit sought to enforce negative covenants on the assumption that the original agreement had been renewed.
The other party had denied the renewal claim, and the claimant did not timely seek a declaration or other relief establishing renewal.
No renewal instrument or court declaration established a subsisting renewed agreement when the injunction suits were filed.
The suits were filed more than three years after the denial of renewal, and the plaints themselves disclosed the relevant events.
issues.conclusion: The injunction claim could not succeed without an established subsisting renewed agreement, and the plaints were properly rejected as barred by limitation.
issues.legal_principle: Enforcement of negative covenants presupposes a subsisting agreement. Because renewal requires an instrument, a party whose renewal claim has been denied must timely seek relief establishing the renewed right; it cannot circumvent the limitation bar by seeking only an injunction based on the assumed renewal. The Court applied Order VII Rule 11(d) of the Code of Civil Procedure and the Limitation Act's three-year limitation applicable to the renewal-related claim. It discussed Article 54 in that context, while assuming without deciding that Article 113 might apply to a suit seeking enforcement of a positive or negative covenant. It also relied on N.V. Srinivasa Murthy v. Mariyamma, T. Arivandandam v. T.V. Satyapal, and I.T.C. Limited v. Debts Recovery Appellate Tribunal.

rule.if: injunction_suit_based_on_renewed_agreement and renewal_claim_denied and no_renewal_instrument_or_declaration and renewal_claim_not_pursued_within_the_limitation_period and application_to_reject_plaint

predicates.injunction_suit_based_on_renewed_agreeme: A claimant brings an injunction suit on the premise that an agreement has been renewed and relies on its covenants.
predicates.renewal_claim_denied: The other party expressly denies that the agreement has been renewed.
predicates.no_renewal_instrument_or_declaration: No renewal instrument or court declaration establishes that the agreement subsists for the further term.
predicates.renewal_claim_not_pursued_within_the_lim: The claimant does not pursue relief establishing renewal within the applicable limitation period after the denial.
predicates.application_to_reject_plaint: A party applies for rejection of the plaint on the ground that the suit is barred by law.

issues.definition: When an injunction suit depends on a renewed agreement that has been denied and not established by an instrument or declaration, and the claimant did not timely pursue relief establishing renewal, the plaint may be rejected as time barred.
